newsitem.title: JAPAN: No threshold level for Japan c/a surplus - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: No threshold level for Japan c/a surplus - Rubin.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Friday there was no level for Japan's current account surplus as a percentage of gross domestic product that the Japanese government should aim to stay below.
Asked if there was such a level, Rubin said, "No."
He was taking questions from U.S. business executives at a meeting of the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan.

Rubin also said it was important that Japan open its markets further, adding that if Japan moved in this direction at a reasonable speed and maintained domestic demand-led growth, the trade surplus issue would take care itself.
"Our view is that if you take the policies, then this (the trade surplus issue) will take care of itself," he said.

When asked about possible policy options for Japan to spur growth in view of current macroeconomic inflexibility, Rubin said: "I don't think we should be prescriptive with respect to Japan any more than the Japanese government should be prescriptive with respect to the U.S."
"I gather that at least one view is that deregulation will be large enough and fast enough to create growth that will offset the fiscal contraction," Rubin added.

"If it happens, then the economy will work its way through this. You'll get the fiscal tightening, you'll get the deregulation and you will not have a resurgence of the current account surplus and all will work out reasonably well," he said.
But he cautioned that if this didn't take place, the result would be a paucity of domestic-led growth and there could be an increase in the current account surplus.
He said that, in that event, the Japanese government would have a number of options with which to deal with the situation, although he refrained from giving specifics.
